config.title: Build worker heartbeat lease mechanism

intro.title: Build worker heartbeat lease mechanism
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a worker heartbeat lease mechanism to monitor the health of background tasks. You will learn how to implement a simple lease system where a worker periodically sends a 'heartbeat' to indicate it is still running. The core programming concept involves using timers and timestamps to track activity and detect failures. You will work with JavaScript's Date object and setInterval for scheduling. This mechanism is a foundational pattern for building reliable distributed systems in Node.js.
intro.usecase: A worker heartbeat lease mechanism is essential in distributed systems where tasks are processed by multiple worker instances, such as in job queues, data processing pipelines, or microservices. For example, in a dashboard that monitors background tasks—like file uploads or report generation—this pattern ensures that if a worker crashes, its lease expires and the task can be reassigned, preventing data loss or stalled processes. Developers implement this in products like video encoding platforms, e-commerce order processing, or real-time analytics systems to maintain reliability and fault tolerance across worker nodes.

objectives: Implement a heartbeat interval that periodically updates worker status
Configure a lease timeout mechanism to detect inactive workers
Construct a lease renewal function that resets the expiration timer
Initialize a worker registry to track active worker leases
Manipulate lease timestamps to calculate remaining active time
Apply conditional logic to determine when a worker lease has expired
Integrate the heartbeat mechanism with worker task execution
Update worker status based on lease expiration events

steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Node.js built-in modules. You'll need these for creating event-driven communication and managing timers.

successCriteria: EventEmitter is imported from 'events', and setTimeout and clearTimeout are imported from 'timers'.

steps.title: Create the HeartbeatManager class skeleton
steps.instruction: Create a new class named HeartbeatManager with a constructor that initializes a workers map and a leaseDuration property.
steps.hint: Define the class using the class keyword, then add a constructor method inside it. Initialize this.workers as a new Map() and this.leaseDuration with a default value (e.g., 30000 for 30 seconds).
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a HeartbeatManager class with a constructor that sets up the workers map and leaseDuration property.
successCriteria: HeartbeatManager class is defined with a constructor that initializes this.workers as a Map and this.leaseDuration as a number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the constructor initializes both this.workers (as a Map) and this.leaseDuration (as a number).

steps.title: Add registerWorker method to HeartbeatManager
steps.instruction: Inside the HeartbeatManager class, add a method named registerWorker that takes a workerId parameter and creates a new Worker instance, storing it in a workers map property (initialize the map in the constructor if needed).
steps.hint: You'll need to create a map to store workers. In the constructor, initialize this.workers = new Map(). Then in registerWorker, create a new Worker and add it to the map using this.workers.set(workerId, worker).
steps.expectedOutcome: The HeartbeatManager class now has a registerWorker method that can create and store Worker instances.
successCriteria: HeartbeatManager has a registerWorker method that creates a new Worker and stores it in a workers map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your registerWorker method creates a new Worker instance and stores it in a map property of the HeartbeatManager class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The registerWorker method isn't implemented correctly. Check that you've added the method to the HeartbeatManager class and it properly creates and stores Worker instances.

steps.expectedOutcome: The HeartbeatManager class will have a removeWorker method that properly cleans up worker resources.
successCriteria: The removeWorker method is defined with a workerId parameter, clears the timeout using clearTimeout, and removes the worker from the workers map using delete.
